title: Transfer from uniform affine étale torsion dimension to the topological-coefficient weak Serre hull
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$, with the discrete topology on $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology on the other rings [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The associated condensed ring is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$ on profinite sets; all continuous functions are used, also for $\Omega$. Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the small-site/indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention], and ordinary internal module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Assume that for every affine étale morphism $v:V\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, and every integer $q>d$, one has $H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0$ [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]. Torsion here is local torsion, without a common annihilator.

Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal P_X$ be the intersection of all replete classes in $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$ containing zero and every finite constant scalar-model constructible module [sk-def-sfb-constructible], closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between members, extensions, and all small ambient coproducts. Extension closure means that if $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ is exact and $M',M''$ belong to the class, so does $M$. Then for every $M\in\mathcal P_X$ and every integer $q>d+2$,
$$H^q\bigl(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M[0])\bigr)=0.$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is the actual right derived functor of global sections of internal $\Lambda_X$-modules to abelian groups. No completion of modules or coefficients is made. No Noetherianity, finite-type structure map to a field, characteristic restriction, invertibility of $\ell$, or finite-subextension-valued replacement of $C(-,\Omega)$ is assumed. Empty $X$, $d=0$, and the zero coefficient ring are included.
